source: arXiv:1610.00278v1, Section 2.2, equation (17) and Lemma 2.7 (PDF/printed p.11); Appendix C Lemma C.2 (p.42)

domains.potential: Original Potential(r): real, mean-zero, physically period-one FL^(s,infinity) distributions. The coefficient-domain theorems hold for arbitrary complex endpoint potentials, without reality, mean-zero or parity assumptions.
domains.physical_domain: The entire original period-two FourierLebesgueSpace 2 1 2, identified by the full original H1/H^-1 duality and actual distributional derivatives. No endpoint regularity premise is imposed on an eigenvector.
domains.rhs_C2: Every original complex period-two FL^(-r,infinity) right-hand side, without mean, reality or parity restrictions.
domains.lambda_C2: Every complex lambda, without strip or tail hypotheses.
domains.endpoint_reduction_weight: Unit spectral weight, exactly the unweighted endpoint scale of the main Birkhoff theorems. Existing arbitrary-weight tail bounds and physical identifications remain available; the new full-domain determinant converse is stated in the unit-weight scale.

quantifier_order: For every admissible r and norm bound R, one N>=1 precedes every original source potential q with norm(q)<=R, every n>=N and every lambda in the corrected strip. The numerical half-contraction proof is produced by the uniform cutoff theorem.
normalization: Period two, modes exp(i*pi*k*x), coefficient q(mode(-k)), free symbol pi^2*k^2, normalized original dual action with factor 1/2. Original distributions and the exact source endpoint norm are preserved.
correction: The shared corrected strip abs(Re(lambda)-pi^2*n^2)<=6*n replaces printed12*n. Actual spectral labels and their eventual inclusion must still be established.
regularity_C2: If (L(q)-lambda)f=g holds as equality of original distributions with f in H1 and g of endpoint order s, an actual original FL^(s+2,infinity) distribution with identical smooth-test action is constructed.
remaining: Analytic parameter family of the endpoint determinant and localization/counting of its zeros.
Actual singular spectrum, spectral labels, algebraic multiplicities and eventual corrected-strip inclusion.
Gap and Dirichlet estimates, inverse spectral regularity, Birkhoff maps and actual KdV main theorem proofs.
qualification: The determinant criterion concerns the physical point eigen-equation, not an asserted equality between the full spectrum and a labeled sequence. The rank bound is geometric; no equality between algebraic multiplicity and determinant-zero order is inferred.
